product_version_reference: Akamai product brief published 03/26; Guardicore Platform Agent 7.2.x line
overall_notes: Guardicore is well documented on discovery, labeling, K8s, SIEM, ServiceNow and process-level enforcement, but publicly available material is thin on quantitative performance numbers (CPU/RAM/latency), HA/DR internals, and formal cryptographic certifications (FIPS/CC).

items.notes: Vendor and third-party sources describe continuous, real-time discovery via lightweight sensors and flow telemetry that build a living application dependency map.
The Reveal map ties each connection to processes and services, giving App / Environment / Role / Process granularity at Layer 7.

items.gaps: Public sources describe rich historical telemetry export but do not state a specific default flow-history retention in days.

items.notes: The Tenable integration brief describes labelling assets with CVE and risk scores and shows CVE labels on assets in the Reveal map for risk-based segmentation.
AI-analyzed flow telemetry surfaces unmanaged assets and non-standard flows, which the platform then presents in the dependency map.
Independent write-ups describe granular policies authored against flexible labels, process, user identity and FQDN, independent of IP/VLAN.
The 2026 AI update to Guardicore automatically generates and explains segmentation policies and simulates impact before enforcement, per Akamai and SiliconAngle coverage.
Guardicore's 'Allow Mode' runs AI-generated policies in simulation showing projected impact before any traffic is blocked.

items.gaps: Public sources reference 'rollback rates' as an operational metric but do not document a documented one-click instant rollback control.
No public description of hierarchical / inherited policy structures was located.

items.notes: Guardicore's 2021 legacy-support release brought coverage for Windows 2000/2003/2008, RHEL 4/5, Solaris SPARC 10/11 and HP-UX 11.23/11.31; current Platform Agent docs list Windows 10-11, Server 2012-2019, RHEL 8+, Debian 11 and Ubuntu 18-22.

Kubernetes enforcement is native via CNI controller with DaemonSet+Helm deployment and a third-party review lists OpenShift OVN among supported CNIs, but the Akamai blog itself notes OpenShift and Cilium support was still being expanded at time of writing.
items.gaps: No authoritative Akamai doc confirming production-ready OpenShift enforcement parity.

items.notes: Guardicore combines agent-based enforcement with agentless visibility via NetFlow/sFlow/IPFIX network collectors, per independent reviews.
The management server is documented for both on-prem and SaaS; support for fully air-gapped operation is not explicitly certified in public sources.
items.gaps: No vendor doc confirms tested air-gapped deployment mode.

items.notes: Akamai cites a global consulting-firm deployment of 300,000 endpoints secured in two weeks, well above the 50,000-workload threshold; the figure is a vendor-attributed customer case.

items.gaps: Public sources describe the agent as 'lightweight' but do not cite a measured CPU percentage under load.
Only macOS memory profile ranges (10 MB soft up to 1000 MB hard limit by host RAM tier) surfaced; that is agent configuration, not measured resident RAM on Windows/Linux at production load.
No public benchmark of added network latency (ms) attributable to the agent was located.
Public documentation and third-party reviews do not describe agent fail-safe behavior when the agent crashes or is stopped (fail-open vs fail-close, traffic continuity).
Vendor techdocs describe silent install and remote upgrade but do not explicitly state whether a reboot is required.

items.notes: Guardicore exposes a REST API used by SIEM add-ons and automation recipes; public sources confirm the API's existence but do not verify 100% coverage of admin console functionality.
items.gaps: No public matrix of REST endpoints versus admin console features.

items.notes: Guardicore telemetry is shipped to Splunk and IBM QRadar via CEF/syslog, with a dedicated Splunkbase add-on that pulls data through the REST API.
A ServiceNow-certified Guardicore application in the ServiceNow Store pulls CMDB data via REST to produce labels for Reveal maps and policies.
Vendor pages mention REST API and automation recipes for DevOps and CI/CD frameworks, but specific Jenkins / GitLab / Terraform module coverage is not detailed in public documents.
items.gaps: No public reference implementation for Jenkins/GitLab/Terraform pipelines.

items.notes: Independent reviews describe the enforcement agent as a process-level Layer 7 firewall that ties each connection to the initiating process.
Guardicore's patented dynamic deception can redirect attackers into a Guardicore-hosted honeypot on anomalous behaviour and records their actions.
Akamai publishes a PCI DSS mapping whitepaper (March 2024) and third parties note NIST SP 800-207 alignment; ready-made ISO 27001 and IEC 62443 reports were not confirmed in public sources.
items.gaps: No public evidence of built-in ISO 27001 or IEC 62443 compliance report packs.

items.notes: Guardicore training material states the agent-to-aggregator connection is encrypted and authenticated on TCP/443 using TLS 1.2; the traffic is authenticated but the checklist's TLS 1.3 requirement is not explicitly met.
items.gaps: No public confirmation of TLS 1.3 support or of mutual (client-certificate) authentication details.
The Centra installation guide references a Scaling Architecture section but the public excerpts do not describe controller HA cluster (active-active / active-passive) topology.
Publicly available material implies local policy decisions on the agent but does not describe explicit autonomous mode when controller connectivity is lost.
The Centra installation guide explicitly notes disaster-recovery setup is not covered in the guide, and no public DR sync procedure was located.
No entry in NIST CMVP or Common Criteria portals for Guardicore was located from public searches; absence of evidence is not evidence of absence.

items.notes: An OT integration with NVIDIA BlueField and Siemens is described as aligning with IEC 62443, which is architectural alignment, not a Siemens/Honeywell/ABB software-compatibility certification for the checklist's target vendors.
items.gaps: No formal Siemens/Honeywell/ABB compatibility certification was located.
